newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Military chief to meet Abacha on Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: Military chief to meet Abacha on Sierra Leone.

text.p: The commander of a West African force assembled in Freetown following last month's army coup in Sierra Leone has arrived in Nigeria to meet Nigerian ruler General Sani Abacha, a government official said on Friday.

"The meeting is very important on the next line of action," said a senior Nigerian official from the capital Abuja where Major-General Victor Malu, the Nigerian commander of the Monrovia-based ECOMOG force was meeting Abacha.
No specific time for their meeting had been set but it was expected to be over the weekend, presidency officials said.
The coup makers, led by Major Johnny Koroma, warned regional power broker Nigeria on Thursday that it would take force to reinstate deposed civilian president Ahmad Tejan Kabbah.
But the coup leaders have also said they want a negotiated settlement to avert a bloody showdown and have sent envoys to President Henri Konan Bedie of Ivory Coast to intervene to find a solution.
The new government in Sierra Leone says it wants to stay in power for 18 months to two years to consolidate the peace it now has with rebels who fought previous governments.
Nigerian gunboats shelled Freetown on Monday in a show of force, while rebels now allied to the coup makers attacked Nigerian troops guarding foreigners at a hotel in Freetown.
"The operation we planned against the Major Johnny Koroma-led rebels has not actually started," Malu told airport reporters on arrival on Thursday.
"I think he is very much scared of what the Nigerian troops in particular can do. I believe this is one of the reasons why he agreed to a ceasefire," the ECOMOG commander said.

Analysts said that for military-ruled Nigeria, the intervention to reinstate democracy in tiny Sierra Leone had become a matter of honour following widespread belief that Monday's fighting was a humiliation for the continent's most populous nation.

"It will be painful if Sierra Leone becomes Nigeria's Vietnam. Not when the enemy is a bunch of rag-tagged rascals on bare feet fighting with antiquated weapons," commented the editor of Thisday newspaper Eziuche Ubani on the front page of his paper on Friday.
Local newspapers also reported that the ECOMOG force in Sierra Leone was now about 4,000-strong.

ECOMOG consists of troops from several West African states although Nigeria forms its backbone. It intervened in the civil war in Liberia, where it currently is in control of security, to police a peace accord brokered by the region's leaders.

The Nigerian-led force has generally received support from home and abroad in its mission to restore democracy in Sierra Leone even though some opposition activists have questioned Nigeria's moral justification when it is itself still under army rule.
Abacha is implementing a transition plan to hand over power next year but the opposition says there is a secret agenda for the general to turn himself into an elected president.
